Every endpoint exposed by the Selector R: Every endpoint exposed by the Selector Registry, with usage guidance, request fields and examples. Client endpoints are called by automation bots; admin endpoints power this UI.
These collections are also exposed as st: These collections are also exposed as standard NocoBase resources supporting list, get, create, update and destroy. Reading needs the "read" snippet; writing needs the "manage" snippet.
Called by automation clients (for exampl: Called by automation clients (for example UiPath robots) over HTTP with an API key. These endpoints use the "client" ACL snippet and are designed to be called on every action and on failure/retry.
Returns the trusted selector for an elem: Returns the trusted selector for an element, and repairs it when a failure is reported.
This is the main endpoint. Call it befor: This is the main endpoint. Call it before an action to get the selector to use (lookup path), and call it again after a failure with the page HTML to trigger self-healing (heal path). Without "failureType" it looks up or bootstraps the entry. With a healable "failureType" plus a "domSnippet", it runs the repair pipeline (heuristics, then LLM) and returns a corrected selector together with fallbacks and a signature. Send "idempotencyKey" so duplicate retries do not double-heal.
Requires the \"client\" capability (snip: Requires the "client" capability (snippet pm.selector-registry.client). Typically an automation bot authenticated by API key.
Registered application name the element: Registered application name the element belongs to.
Stable identity of the element. Provide: Stable identity of the element. Provide either "elementKey" or "logicalId". Use a stable value such as "workflowId:stepId".
Human-readable logical id. Hashed with a: Human-readable logical id. Hashed with app and page into the elementKey when elementKey is not given.
Optional display name stored on the entr: Optional display name stored on the entry.

The selector the client currently holds: The selector the client currently holds or used. Used for the cache hit check and as the starting point for healing.
Selector type. Defaults to \"css\". Only: Selector type. Defaults to "css". Only CSS selectors can be validated server-side.
Present to report a failure and trigger: Present to report a failure and trigger healing. "not_interactable" and "page_error" are treated as dirty evidence and never heal.
Optional error text from the automation: Optional error text from the automation client, used for logging and LLM context.
HTML snapshot of the page (or the region: HTML snapshot of the page (or the region around the element). Required for healing. Large pages are trimmed to the configured limit.
Optional client-provided candidates: { s: Optional client-provided candidates: { selector } or { tag, attrs } or { text }. Validated and ranked during healing.
Optional selectors already attempted, so: Optional selectors already attempted, so they are not suggested again.
Optional identifier of the bot/agent mak: Optional identifier of the bot/agent making the request.
Optional key (for example \"runId:stepId: Optional key (for example "runId:stepId") to reuse a recent identical response and avoid duplicate heals.
Returns the resolved selector and metada: Returns the resolved selector and metadata: "source" (cache_hit | registry | heuristic | llm | miss | skipped), "selector", "selectorType", "version", "status", "confidence", "healTriggered", "fallbacks" (previous selectors to try), and "signature" (to verify the element client-side). When "source" is "miss" and no selector is known, fall back to your workflow default selector.
Reports whether the selector worked, so: Reports whether the selector worked, so the registry can learn and stabilise.
Call this after every action with the ou: Call this after every action with the outcome. This feedback loop is required for the system to stabilise: successes raise confidence and promote "probation" entries to "active"; failures lower confidence and can degrade, quarantine, or auto-rollback to the last proven selector. Without reporting, healed selectors stay on probation and the registry cannot learn.
The element identity returned by resolve: The element identity returned by resolve.
What happened when the selector was used: What happened when the selector was used. "verified"/"mismatch" come from signature verification.
The selector actually used, to attribute: The selector actually used, to attribute the outcome to the right version.
If outcome is fail/mismatch, the type of: If outcome is fail/mismatch, the type of failure.
Whether the located element matched the: Whether the located element matched the stored signature.
Returns the updated entry summary (statu: Returns the updated entry summary (status, confidence, version). Check the entry status to know if it was promoted, degraded, or rolled back.
Syncs a local cache efficiently: send wh: Syncs a local cache efficiently: send what you have, receive only what changed.
Use this at the start of a run to refres: Use this at the start of a run to refresh a local cache that covers many steps at once, instead of calling resolve per step. Send the elementKeys and versions currently cached; the registry replies with the entries that changed ("updates"), the keys it does not know ("unknown"), and a count of entries that are unchanged. Apply "updates" to your local cache and keep your own value for "unknown".
List of { elementKey, version? } current: List of { elementKey, version? } currently held in the local cache. Up to 500 items per call.
Returns { app, updates, unknown, unchang: Returns { app, updates, unknown, unchanged }. "updates" is a list of full entry payloads (same shape as resolve responses); "unknown" lists elementKeys the registry does not know; "unchanged" is a count.
Used by the administration UI and by ope: Used by the administration UI and by operators. Read actions need the "read" snippet; mutating actions need the "manage" snippet.

Send only the fields to change; unspecif: Send only the fields to change; unspecified fields keep their current value. Numeric fields must be finite and non-negative. The full list of settings and their meaning is documented on the Settings tab of this plugin.

Returns { entries, apps, recentResolves,: Returns { entries, apps, recentResolves, recentFeedback, topFailing }.
Previews what self-healing would do for: Previews what self-healing would do for one entry, without changing live state.
Re-runs the healing pipeline for a singl: Re-runs the healing pipeline for a single entry in forced dry-run mode.
